title: How a prediction request flows

nodes.label: Next.js dashboard
nodes.note: Frontend/ app: login, model upload, API keys, sharing, webhooks and analytics pages. Talks to the API through lib/api-client.ts.

nodes.label: API consumers
nodes.note: Any app calling POST /predictions/{model_id} with an X-API-Key header instead of a browser session.

nodes.label: Middleware stack
nodes.note: core/middleware.py plus CORS and session middleware: error tracking, slow-request timing, request logging, rate-limit headers.

nodes.label: Auth dependencies
nodes.note: api/dependencies.py: get_current_user accepts a JWT bearer token or an X-API-Key (SHA-256 hash lookup), plus admin and per-model share checks.

nodes.label: Routers (v1)
nodes.note: api/v1: auth, models, predictions, api_keys, model_shares, webhooks, users, health. About 37 route handlers, validated with Pydantic.

nodes.label: Rate limiter
nodes.note: core/rate_limiter.py: a Depends(rate_limit(config)) per route, using a Redis sorted-set sliding window. Fails open if Redis is down.

nodes.label: Prediction cache
nodes.note: core/caching.py: keys pred:{model}:{version}:{sha256 of input}, 1 hour TTL, hit and miss stats, per-model invalidation.

nodes.label: Model loader
nodes.note: core/model_loader.py: loads joblib or pickle models and keeps up to 5 in an in-process cache so repeat misses skip the disk or S3 read.

nodes.label: Storage service
nodes.note: core/storage.py: one interface for S3 and local disk. Used by the upload route to save models and by the loader to read them.

nodes.label: Background tasks
nodes.note: FastAPI BackgroundTasks, run after the response: cache the result, write the prediction log, trigger webhooks.

nodes.label: Webhook dispatcher
nodes.note: core/webhook_service.py: signs the payload with HMAC-SHA256, POSTs it with httpx and retries on 5xx or network errors.

nodes.label: Redis
nodes.note: Holds pred:* cached predictions and rate_limit:* sorted sets. Both degrade gracefully when Redis is not configured.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL
nodes.note: SQLAlchemy models for users, models and versions, API keys, model shares, webhooks and predictions. Schema managed with Alembic.

nodes.label: S3 or local disk
nodes.note: Serialized model files. S3 via boto3 when configured, otherwise the UPLOAD_DIR folder.

nodes.label: Customer webhook URL
nodes.note: Receives events with X-Webhook-Signature, X-Webhook-Timestamp and X-Webhook-Id headers.

nodes.label: Google and GitHub OAuth
nodes.note: services/oauth.py registers both providers with authlib for the /auth/oauth/{provider} login flow.

flow: A client POSTs input to /predictions/{model_id}, either from the dashboard with a JWT or from an app with an X-API-Key.
The middleware stack logs and times the request, then get_current_user resolves the caller from the token or the hashed key in PostgreSQL.
The route's rate limit is checked in Redis with a sliding window; over the limit returns 429.
The model record is loaded from PostgreSQL, the input is hashed, and Redis is checked for a cached prediction. A hit returns immediately.
On a miss the model loader reads the file through the storage service (or its in-memory cache), runs predict and returns the result.
After the response, background tasks write the result to Redis with a one hour TTL and log the prediction to PostgreSQL.
Secondary path: the same tasks call trigger_webhooks, which POSTs an HMAC-SHA256 signed event to each registered URL and retries on failure.
